source_quote: T1 treatments lethalities were closer to 1 log CFU/mL when the UVC dose was of 80 J/mL and above, being maximum (1.2 log CFU/mL) after a dose of 160 J/mL.
notes: Spores inoculated at ~6 log CFU/mL in skim milk; 254 nm UV-C in a concentric tubular reactor, T1 = single pass (NET low). Value is the maximum lethality for T1.

source_quote: When a single pass through the reactor was used (T1), lethality was always below 1 log CFU/mL, and no significant differences ( p ≥ 0.05) were observed between UVC doses.
notes: Whole milk, T1 (single pass): the paper states only that lethality was always below 1 log CFU/mL with no significant differences between doses (20-160 J/mL); per-dose values exist only in Figure 2, so response_value is null. dose_value 160 J/mL is the highest dose covered by the statement.

source_quote: The most effective treatment in whole milk showed to be the T3, being necessary a dose of 91.2 J/mL to inactivate 4 log CFU/mL of spores, but the difference with the T2 treatments was small.
notes: 4D_UVC value: UV-C dose estimated (Weibull-with-tail fit, GInaFiT) to give a 4 log10 CFU/mL reduction with the T3 recirculation treatment. Derived by the authors from the fitted inactivation curve, hence evidence_level=inferred.

source_quote: On the contrary, T3 treatments showed to be much more efficient in skim milk, where a dose of 41.6 J/mL would be enough to achieve this goal.
notes: 4D_UVC value: UV-C dose estimated (Weibull-with-tail fit, GInaFiT) to give a 4 log10 CFU/mL reduction with the T3 recirculation treatment. Derived by the authors from the fitted inactivation curve, hence evidence_level=inferred.
